title: 12.21 Elliptic surface volumes and order spectra
search_title: Elliptic surface volumes and order spectra
section: 12.21 Elliptic surface volumes and order spectra
text: On a product of two elliptic curves, a semipositive background whose coefficients depend on one factor only has an explicit volume. Solving the smooth equation reduces to a Poisson equation on that factor, and the volume of each Hermitian perturbation is governed by the harmonic mean of the perturbed vertical coefficient. The rate at which this coefficient vanishes therefore determines the order of degeneration. Zeros of finite order give fractional orders or logarithmic decay, while coefficients that vanish to infinite order can make the logarithmic rate oscillate. Let $E=\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+\mathrm{i}\mathbb Z)$, write $X=E_ z\times E_ w$, and fix \[  \omega _1=\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\mathrm{d} z\wedge \mathrm{d}\bar z,\qquad \omega _2=\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\mathrm{d} w\wedge \mathrm{d}\bar w,\qquad \mu =\omega _1\wedge \omega _2,\qquad h=\omega _1+\omega _2.  \] Both area forms have integral one. Let $a,q,r$ be smooth functions of $z$ alone, with $a,q$ real and nonnegative, $r$ complex-valued, and $|r|^2\leq aq$. Set \[  \theta =\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\bigl (a\, \mathrm{d} z\wedge \mathrm{d}\bar z+ r\, \mathrm{d} z\wedge \mathrm{d}\bar w+\bar r\, \mathrm{d} w\wedge \mathrm{d}\bar z+ q\, \mathrm{d} w\wedge \mathrm{d}\bar w\bigr ).  \] This is a smooth semipositive form, and in particular it is nef. Proposition 12.21.1 . DE2BA13B1A92 For $\epsilon >0$, put $g=q+\epsilon $ and $I=\int _ Eg^{-1}\omega _1$. Then 5C3988BE0A59 12.21.2 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) =\frac{2}{I}\left(\int _ E(a+\epsilon )\omega _1- \int _ E\frac{|r|^2}{g}\omega _1\right), \end{equation} and the infimum defining this volume is attained by a smooth positive Gauduchon metric. In particular, if $a$ is a constant $b>0$ and $r=0$, then $\mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)=2(b+\epsilon )/I$. If $|r|^2=aq$, then A72D1E62A49B 12.21.3 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)=\frac{2\epsilon (1+K)}{I}, \qquad K=\int _ E\frac{a}{q+\epsilon }\omega _1. \end{equation} Proof. Define \[  c=I^{-1}\left(\int _ E(a+\epsilon )\omega _1- \int _ E\frac{|r|^2}{g}\omega _1\right),\qquad A=\frac{c+|r|^2}{g}.  \] Since $(a+\epsilon )g-|r|^2>0$, we have $c>0$, and the definition of $c$ makes $A-a-\epsilon $ have zero mean with respect to $\omega _1$. Dividing its nonconstant Fourier coefficients by the corresponding nonzero eigenvalues of the flat Laplacian produces a smooth real function $u$ on $E$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=(A-a-\epsilon )\omega _1$. Pull it back to $X$. The form $\Omega =\theta +\epsilon h+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ has coefficient matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A& r\\ \bar r& g\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, which has determinant $c$ and positive diagonal entries. Hence $\Omega >0$ and $\Omega ^2=2c\mu $, and theorem 12.2.3 gives ( 12.21.2 ). The metric $\gamma _*=\Omega /g$ has constant coefficient $1$ in the fiber direction, and its remaining coefficients depend only on $z$. Applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to its base term or its mixed terms produces a repeated $\mathrm{d} z$ or $\mathrm{d}\bar z$, so $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\gamma _*=0$. Thus $\gamma _*$ is a smooth Gauduchon metric conformal to $\Omega $, and by theorem 12.2.3 it attains the infimum. The two special cases follow by direct substitution. $\square$ Proposition 12.21.4 . 58574FAEC5B7 For each integer $m>1$ there is a smooth semipositive nonclosed form on $X$ with common order $1-1/m$. For each $b>0$ there is also one with \[  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)\sim \frac{2b}{\pi \log (1/\epsilon )} \quad (\epsilon \downarrow 0);  \] it has volume zero and both orders zero. Proof. In proposition 12.21.1 take $a=b>0$ and $r=0$. Fix a point $z_0\in E$ and a flat coordinate $\zeta =z-z_0$ on a small disk about $z_0$. Choose $q$ smooth, positive outside $z_0$, and equal to $|\zeta |^{2m}$ on that disk; a positive smooth extension exists away from the disk. For $m=1$, polar coordinates give \[  I=\int _ E\frac{\omega _1}{q+\epsilon } =\pi \log (1/\epsilon )+O(1),  \] and ( 12.21.2 ) gives the asymptotic formula of the statement. If $m>1$, the substitution $s=|\zeta |^2=\epsilon ^{1/m}t$ gives \[  I\sim C_ m\epsilon ^{1/m-1},\qquad C_ m=\pi \int _0^\infty \frac{\mathrm{d} t}{1+t^ m}>0,  \] so the common order is $1-1/m$. In the logarithmic case, $\lambda _\mu (\theta )\geq 0$ by semipositivity, while $\lambda _\mu (\theta )\leq \lambda _\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)\to 0$ by monotonicity; hence $\mathcal V_\mu (\theta )=0$. Moreover, the quotient of the volume by $\epsilon ^\delta $ diverges for every $\delta >0$, so both orders vanish. Finally, $\mathrm{d}\theta =\mathrm{d} q\wedge \omega _2\ne 0$, so these backgrounds are not closed. $\square$ Proposition 12.21.5 . 41097C9AFBD2 For every $0<\alpha <\beta <1$ there is a smooth semipositive nonclosed background on $X$, with the same $\mu $ and $h$, such that \[  \bigl (\underline a(\theta ),\overline a(\theta )\bigr ) =(1+\alpha ,1+\beta ).  \] For every $0<\sigma <1$ there is such a background with common order $1+\sigma $. Proof. We use the rank-one formula ( 12.21.3 ), with coefficients that vanish to infinite order at one point at a prescribed oscillating rate. Step 1: the coefficients. For all sufficiently large $t$, define \[  p(t)=\frac{\alpha +\beta }{2} +\frac{\beta -\alpha }{2}\sin (\log \log t),\qquad P(t)=tp(t).  \] Choose $T$ so large that $0<c_0\leq P'(t)\leq d_0<1$ for $t\geq T$; this is possible because \[  P'(t)=p(t)+\frac{\beta -\alpha }{2\log t}\cos (\log \log t)  \] and $\alpha \leq p\leq \beta $. Fix $z_0\in E$ and a flat coordinate $\zeta $ centered at $z_0$. On $E\setminus \{ z_0\} $ choose a smooth function $t(z)\geq T$ that equals $|\zeta |^{-2}$ near $z_0$ and is bounded outside every neighborhood of $z_0$. Put \[  q=\mathrm{e}^{-t},\qquad a=\mathrm{e}^{-P(t)},\qquad r=\mathrm{e}^{-(P(t)+t)/2},  \] and set all three equal to zero at $z_0$. These functions are smooth and vanish to infinite order at $z_0$: we have $P(t)\geq \alpha t$, and every fixed derivative of $P$ grows at most polynomially in $t$, so by the chain rule each coordinate derivative is bounded by a polynomial in $|\zeta |^{-1}$ times $\mathrm{e}^{-c/|\zeta |^2}$ for some $c>0$. Since $|r|^2=aq$, the resulting $\theta $ is semipositive. It is not closed: the component $\mathrm{d} q\wedge \omega _2$ of $\mathrm{d}\theta $ contains both fiber differentials, and derivatives of the remaining terms cannot cancel it. Step 2: asymptotics of $I$ and $K$. Write $\epsilon =\mathrm{e}^{-L}$, and let $T_0\geq T$ be such that $t=|\zeta |^{-2}$ on the disk $\{ |\zeta |^2<1/T_0\} $. Outside this disk the integrands of $I$ and $K$ in ( 12.21.3 ) are bounded, so their contributions are $O(1)$, while polar coordinates on the disk give \[  I_{\mathrm{loc}}=\pi \int _{T_0}^\infty \frac{t^{-2}\, \mathrm{d} t}{\mathrm{e}^{-t}+\mathrm{e}^{-L}},\qquad K_{\mathrm{loc}}=\pi \int _{T_0}^\infty \frac{\mathrm{e}^{-P(t)}t^{-2}\, \mathrm{d} t}{\mathrm{e}^{-t}+\mathrm{e}^{-L}}.  \] The part of $I_{\mathrm{loc}}$ over $t\geq L$ is at least a fixed multiple of $\mathrm{e}^ L/L$. For an upper bound, use $(\mathrm{e}^{-t}+\mathrm{e}^{-L})^{-1}\leq \mathrm{e}^ t$ for $t\leq L$ and $(\mathrm{e}^{-t}+\mathrm{e}^{-L})^{-1}\leq \mathrm{e}^ L$ for $t\geq L$, and split $[T_0,L]$ at $L/2$. Splitting the integral for $K$ at $t=L$ therefore gives $K\leq C\mathrm{e}^{L-P(L)}$. If instead $P(t)=\sigma t$, the same smoothness and integral estimates give the common order $1+\sigma $. In particular, $\sigma =\sqrt2-1$ gives an irrational common order. $\square$

title: Proposition 12.21.1
section: 12.21 Elliptic surface volumes and order spectra
text: Proposition 12.21.1 . DE2BA13B1A92 For $\epsilon >0$, put $g=q+\epsilon $ and $I=\int _ Eg^{-1}\omega _1$. Then 5C3988BE0A59 12.21.2 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) =\frac{2}{I}\left(\int _ E(a+\epsilon )\omega _1- \int _ E\frac{|r|^2}{g}\omega _1\right), \end{equation} and the infimum defining this volume is attained by a smooth positive Gauduchon metric. In particular, if $a$ is a constant $b>0$ and $r=0$, then $\mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)=2(b+\epsilon )/I$. If $|r|^2=aq$, then A72D1E62A49B 12.21.3 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)=\frac{2\epsilon (1+K)}{I}, \qquad K=\int _ E\frac{a}{q+\epsilon }\omega _1. \end{equation} Proof. Define \[  c=I^{-1}\left(\int _ E(a+\epsilon )\omega _1- \int _ E\frac{|r|^2}{g}\omega _1\right),\qquad A=\frac{c+|r|^2}{g}.  \] Since $(a+\epsilon )g-|r|^2>0$, we have $c>0$, and the definition of $c$ makes $A-a-\epsilon $ have zero mean with respect to $\omega _1$. Dividing its nonconstant Fourier coefficients by the corresponding nonzero eigenvalues of the flat Laplacian produces a smooth real function $u$ on $E$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=(A-a-\epsilon )\omega _1$. Pull it back to $X$. The form $\Omega =\theta +\epsilon h+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ has coefficient matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A& r\\ \bar r& g\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, which has determinant $c$ and positive diagonal entries. Hence $\Omega >0$ and $\Omega ^2=2c\mu $, and theorem 12.2.3 gives ( 12.21.2 ). The metric $\gamma _*=\Omega /g$ has constant coefficient $1$ in the fiber direction, and its remaining coefficients depend only on $z$. Thus $\gamma _*$ is a smooth Gauduchon metric conformal to $\Omega $, and by theorem 12.2.3 it attains the infimum. The two special cases follow by direct substitution. $\square$

title: 12.22 Comparison under an arbitrary modification
text: The orders of degeneration are defined on a fixed manifold. We now show that pulling a nef background back by a modification can only increase them. Recall that a modification $\pi :Y\to X$ is a proper surjective holomorphic map that restricts to a biholomorphism between dense Zariski open subsets. The proof compares Gauduchon tests on $X$ with tests on $Y$. The pullback of a Gauduchon test is degenerate along the exceptional locus, and adding a small positive test on $Y$ repairs this. To control the effect of the added test uniformly, we first bound the pairing of pulled-back tests with a Hermitian form on $Y$ by their pairing with a Hermitian form on $X$, uniformly over the whole cone of tests. In this subsection $\pi :Y\to X$ is a modification of connected compact complex manifolds of dimension $n\geq 2$. We use Hironaka's analytic elimination of indeterminacies in the following form: there are a finite composition $p:Z\to X$ of blowups along smooth centers and a modification $F:Z\to Y$ with $p=\pi \circ F$. It is obtained by resolving the indeterminacies of the inverse meromorphic map $\pi ^{-1}\circ p$; the identity $p=\pi \circ F$ holds on the dense set where the maps are biholomorphic, hence everywhere. This classical input is discussed in section 25.17 . For an effective real divisor $D$, we write $\eta _ D$ for the curvature form of a smooth Hermitian metric on the corresponding real line bundle, as in section 12.35 . Lemma 12.22.1 . 0A017BFF9468 Let $p:Z\to X$ be a finite composition of blowups along smooth centers of codimension at least two, and let $h_ X$ be a Hermitian form on $X$. There are a constant $C_0>0$, an effective real divisor $D$ on $Z$ whose components are exceptional for $p$, and a smooth curvature form $\eta _ D$ such that 1427E28847CB 12.22.2 \begin{equation}  h_ Z=C_0p^*h_ X-\eta _ D>0. \end{equation} Every component of $D$ is mapped by $p$ into a set of complex codimension at least two in $X$. Proof. First let $q:M'\to M$ be one blowup along a smooth center, with exceptional divisor $E$, and let $h_ M$ be a Hermitian form on $M$. The restriction of $\mathcal O(-E)$ to each projective fiber of $E$ is $\mathcal O(1)$. A Hermitian metric on the normal bundle of the center therefore induces a metric on $\mathcal O(-E)|_ E$ whose curvature is positive on the tangent spaces of the fibers. Extend this metric to $\mathcal O(-E)$ on $M'$ by extending the smooth logarithm of its ratio to a fixed reference metric from the closed submanifold $E$, and let $\beta $ be its curvature. The semipositive form $q^*h_ M$ is positive off $E$, and at points of $E$ its kernel is exactly the tangent space of the fiber, on which $\beta $ is positive. Hence $Cq^*h_ M+\beta >0$ for every sufficiently large $C$: otherwise, unit tangent vectors violating the inequality for $C\to \infty $ would converge, by compactness, to a vector in the kernel of $q^*h_ M$ on which $\beta $ is nonpositive. With $\eta _ E=-\beta $, the curvature of the induced metric on $\mathcal O(E)$, this reads $Cq^*h_ M-\eta _ E>0$. For a composition of blowups, apply this step successively, with $h_ M$ the positive form already obtained on the previous blowup. Each step multiplies the previous divisor by a positive constant, pulls it back and adds the new exceptional divisor, so the divisor stays effective and exceptional. This proves ( 12.22.2 ). Each exceptional divisor maps into the image of its center, which has dimension at most $n-2$. $\square$ Lemma 12.22.3 . 51797AE0DE1F Fix Hermitian forms $h_ X,h_ Y$ for a modification $\pi :Y\to X$. There is a constant $K>0$ such that 3145A1C49A8A 12.22.4 \begin{equation}  \int _ Y h_ Y\wedge \pi ^*\Psi \leq K\int _ X h_ X\wedge \Psi \end{equation} for every smooth strictly positive $(n-1,n-1)$-form $\Psi $ on $X$ with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Psi =0$. Proof. Use the factorization $p=\pi \circ F$ above and lemma 12.22.1 . By compactness there is $a>0$ with $h_ Z\geq aF^*h_ Y$. Pulling back the semipositive form $\Psi $ and integrating, we obtain \[  a\int _ Yh_ Y\wedge \pi ^*\Psi \leq \int _ Zh_ Z\wedge p^*\Psi =C_0\int _ Xh_ X\wedge \Psi -\int _ Dp^*\Psi .  \] Here the changes of variables use that $F$ and $p$ have degree one, and the Poincaré–Lelong formula, together with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}p^*\Psi =0$, replaces the pairing with $\eta _ D$ by the integral over $D$. This last integral vanishes: on the regular locus of each component of $D$, the restriction of $p$ has rank at most $n-2$, so the restriction of the $(n-1,n-1)$-form $p^*\Psi $ is zero. Taking $K=C_0/a$ proves the assertion. $\square$ Proposition 12.22.5 . 8AB4DFD2719F Let $\pi :Y\to X$ be a modification of connected compact complex manifolds of dimension $n\geq 2$, and let $\theta $ be a smooth nef background on $X$. Then $\pi ^*\theta $ is nef. For fixed Hermitian forms $h_ X,h_ Y$ and smooth positive probability forms $\mu _ X,\mu _ Y$, there are constants $C,K>0$, independent of $\epsilon $, such that 2D24229F8C67 12.22.6 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_{\mu _ Y}(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y) \leq C\mathcal V_{\mu _ X}(\theta +K\epsilon h_ X) \qquad (\epsilon >0). \end{equation} Consequently \[  \underline a(\pi ^*\theta )\geq \underline a(\theta ),\qquad \overline a(\pi ^*\theta )\geq \overline a(\theta ).  \] In dimension one a modification is an isomorphism and preserves both orders. Proof. Step 1: nefness. Choose $C'$ with $\pi ^*h_ X\leq C'h_ Y$. For $\epsilon >0$, pull back a smooth representative $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_\tau \geq -\tau h_ X$ with $\tau <\epsilon /C'$; this gives a positive representative of $\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y$. Thus $\pi ^*\theta $ is nef, and both volumes in ( 12.22.6 ) are positive. Step 2: regularized tests. The ratio $\pi ^*\mu _ X/\mu _ Y$ is smooth, nonnegative and bounded on the compact manifold $Y$, so there is $c>0$ with $\mu _ Y\geq c\pi ^*\mu _ X$. Fix a smooth Gauduchon metric $\gamma _0$ on $Y$, given by theorem 11.4.2 . For an arbitrary Gauduchon metric $\gamma $ on $X$, write $\Psi =\gamma ^{n-1}$, and for $\delta >0$ define $\Gamma _\delta $ by \[  \Gamma _\delta ^{n-1}=\pi ^*\Psi +\delta \gamma _0^{n-1}.  \] The right side is a strictly positive $(n-1,n-1)$-form, and such a form has a unique smooth positive $(n-1)$st root, obtained by solving for the Hermitian matrix of the root from the positive cofactor matrix. Since the right side is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-closed, $\Gamma _\delta $ is a smooth Gauduchon metric on $Y$. Step 3: the numerator. For $\epsilon >0$, lemma 12.22.3 gives C7A393B9C4B8 12.22.7 \begin{equation}  \lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}\int _ Y(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y) \wedge \Gamma _\delta ^{n-1} =\int _ X\theta \wedge \Psi +\epsilon \int _ Yh_ Y\wedge \pi ^*\Psi \leq \int _ X(\theta +K\epsilon h_ X)\wedge \Psi . \end{equation} The first term in the middle is nonnegative because $\theta $ is nef, and the second is positive because $\pi ^*\Psi $ is positive on the set where $\pi $ is biholomorphic, so the limit is positive. Step 4: the denominator. We claim that 1419E4EEEE39 12.22.8 \begin{equation}  \lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}D_{\mu _ Y}(\Gamma _\delta ) =\int _ Y(\pi ^*\gamma ^ n)^{(n-1)/n}\mu _ Y^{1/n} \geq c^{1/n}D_{\mu _ X}(\gamma )>0. \end{equation} To justify the limit on the exceptional locus, represent $\Gamma _\delta ^{n-1}$ by its positive cofactor matrix. The density of $(\Gamma _\delta ^ n)^{(n-1)/n}$ is a fixed dimensional constant times the $1/n$th power of the determinant of that matrix, and this expression extends continuously to positive semidefinite matrices. Since $Y$ is compact, dominated convergence applies. The inequality follows from $\mu _ Y\geq c\pi ^*\mu _ X$ and the change of variables for the degree-one map $\pi $. Step 5: conclusion. Test the infimum defining $\lambda _{\mu _ Y}(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y)$ with $\Gamma _\delta $, use ( 12.22.7 ) and ( 12.22.8 ), and let $\delta \downarrow 0$. For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $ on $X$ this gives \[  \lambda _{\mu _ Y}(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y) \leq c^{-1/n} \frac{\int _ X(\theta +K\epsilon h_ X)\wedge \gamma ^{n-1}}{D_{\mu _ X}(\gamma )}.  \] Taking the infimum over $\gamma $ and then the $n$th power proves ( 12.22.6 ) with $C=c^{-1}$. Dividing the logarithm of ( 12.22.6 ) by $\log \epsilon <0$ reverses the inequality. The bounded error $\log C$ and the rescaling $\epsilon \mapsto K\epsilon $ do not affect lower and upper limits, as in the proof of proposition 12.20.1 . This gives $\underline a(\pi ^*\theta )\geq \underline a(\theta )$ and $\overline a(\pi ^*\theta )\geq \overline a(\theta )$. Finally, a proper holomorphic map of degree one between compact Riemann surfaces is an isomorphism, which settles the case $n=1$. $\square$

The ratio $\pi ^*\mu _ X/\mu _ Y$ is smooth, nonnegative and bounded on the compact manifold $Y$, so there is $c>0$ with $\mu _ Y\geq c\pi ^*\mu _ X$. For an arbitrary Gauduchon metric $\gamma $ on $X$, write $\Psi =\gamma ^{n-1}$, and for $\delta >0$ define $\Gamma _\delta $ by \[  \Gamma _\delta ^{n-1}=\pi ^*\Psi +\delta \gamma _0^{n-1}.  \] The right side is a strictly positive $(n-1,n-1)$-form, and such a form has a unique smooth positive $(n-1)$st root, obtained by solving for the Hermitian matrix of the root from the positive cofactor matrix. Since the right side is $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-closed, $\Gamma _\delta $ is a smooth Gauduchon metric on $Y$. Step 3: the numerator. For $\epsilon >0$, lemma 12.22.3 gives C7A393B9C4B8 12.22.7 \begin{equation}  \lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}\int _ Y(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y) \wedge \Gamma _\delta ^{n-1} =\int _ X\theta \wedge \Psi +\epsilon \int _ Yh_ Y\wedge \pi ^*\Psi \leq \int _ X(\theta +K\epsilon h_ X)\wedge \Psi . \end{equation} The first term in the middle is nonnegative because $\theta $ is nef, and the second is positive because $\pi ^*\Psi $ is positive on the set where $\pi $ is biholomorphic, so the limit is positive. Step 4: the denominator. We claim that 1419E4EEEE39 12.22.8 \begin{equation}  \lim _{\delta \downarrow 0}D_{\mu _ Y}(\Gamma _\delta ) =\int _ Y(\pi ^*\gamma ^ n)^{(n-1)/n}\mu _ Y^{1/n} \geq c^{1/n}D_{\mu _ X}(\gamma )>0. \end{equation} To justify the limit on the exceptional locus, represent $\Gamma _\delta ^{n-1}$ by its positive cofactor matrix. The density of $(\Gamma _\delta ^ n)^{(n-1)/n}$ is a fixed dimensional constant times the $1/n$th power of the determinant of that matrix, and this expression extends continuously to positive semidefinite matrices. Since $Y$ is compact, dominated convergence applies. The inequality follows from $\mu _ Y\geq c\pi ^*\mu _ X$ and the change of variables for the degree-one map $\pi $. Step 5: conclusion. Test the infimum defining $\lambda _{\mu _ Y}(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y)$ with $\Gamma _\delta $, use ( 12.22.7 ) and ( 12.22.8 ), and let $\delta \downarrow 0$. For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $ on $X$ this gives \[  \lambda _{\mu _ Y}(\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y) \leq c^{-1/n} \frac{\int _ X(\theta +K\epsilon h_ X)\wedge \gamma ^{n-1}}{D_{\mu _ X}(\gamma )}.  \] Taking the infimum over $\gamma $ and then the $n$th power proves ( 12.22.6 ) with $C=c^{-1}$. Finally, a proper holomorphic map of degree one between compact Riemann surfaces is an isomorphism, which settles the case $n=1$. $\square$

title: 12.24 Positive-current subtraction and divisorial residuals
text: Another way to change the order of degeneration is to subtract a positive current from the background. If $\theta -\beta $ differs from a positive current by a $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-exact term, then every Gauduchon pairing of $\theta $ dominates the corresponding pairing of $\beta $. When the residual $\beta $ is still nef, its perturbed volumes are therefore smaller, and its orders are at least those of $\theta $. The main example is the subtraction of the curvature form of an effective divisor. Such a subtraction can preserve the order, raise it by an integer or by a fraction, or produce unequal lower and upper orders; and the residual need not be nef. Proposition 12.24.1 . 7CE9EDC18591 Let $\theta ,\beta $ be smooth nef real $(1,1)$-forms on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and suppose that \[  S=(\theta -\beta )+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq 0  \] is a positive $(1,1)$-current for some integrable function $\varphi $. For every Hermitian form $h$, every smooth strictly positive probability form $\mu $ and every $\epsilon >0$, 2818CCA10129 12.24.2 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_\mu (\beta +\epsilon h)\leq \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h). \end{equation} Consequently $\underline a(\beta )\geq \underline a(\theta )$ and $\overline a(\beta )\geq \overline a(\theta )$. Proof. For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $, distributional integration by parts gives \[  \int _ X(\theta -\beta )\wedge \gamma ^{n-1} =\langle S,\gamma ^{n-1}\rangle \geq 0.  \] Hence, for each test metric, the quotient for $\theta +\epsilon h$ is at least the quotient for $\beta +\epsilon h$, and taking infima gives $\lambda _\mu (\beta +\epsilon h)\leq \lambda _\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)$. Both sides are positive because $\beta $ and $\theta $ are nef, so raising to the $n$th power gives ( 12.24.2 ). Dividing the logarithms by the negative number $\log \epsilon $ reverses the inequality and proves both comparisons of orders. $\square$ For an effective real divisor $D$ with curvature form $\eta _ D$, the Poincaré–Lelong formula gives $[D]=\eta _ D+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ for a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $\varphi $. Thus proposition 12.24.1 applies to $\beta =\theta -\eta _ D$, with $S=[D]$, whenever $\beta $ is nef. For a convergent countable positive combination of divisors, the same argument applies only when its curvature representative is smooth and a global potential realizes the current difference. If $T=\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ is a positive current with $T-S\geq 0$, then $T-S=\beta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u-\varphi )$, so $\beta $ is the background of the positive current that remains after $S$ is removed from $T$. Proposition 12.24.3 . D15FEB2692E7 Subtracting the curvature form of an effective divisor from a smooth nef background, with a smooth nef residual, can preserve the common order, raise it by any integer between $1$ and the dimension or by a fraction, or produce a residual whose lower and upper orders differ. The residual can also fail to be nef. Proof. Integer jumps. On $E^ n$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, let $\omega _ i$ be the pullback of a flat area form of integral one from the $i$th factor, and set $h=\sum _ i\omega _ i$ and $\mu =\omega _1\wedge \cdots \wedge \omega _ n$. The divisor $F_ i$ obtained by fixing a point in the $i$th factor has $\omega _ i$ as a smooth curvature form: on that elliptic curve, any curvature form of the corresponding line bundle differs from $\omega _ i$ by $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ of a solution of a zero-mean Poisson equation, so the metric can be adjusted, and then pulled back. For $\theta =h$ and $D=\sum _{i=1}^ kF_ i$, the residual $\beta =\sum _{i=k+1}^ n\omega _ i$ is smooth and nef. The perturbed forms are closed, positive and of constant density with respect to $\mu $, so the zero potential solves their equations, and theorem 12.2.3 gives D74CAC12DD59 12.24.4 \begin{equation}  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)=n!(1+\epsilon )^ n,\qquad \mathcal V_\mu (\beta +\epsilon h)=n!\epsilon ^ k(1+\epsilon )^{n-k}. \end{equation} For $n=1$ the same formula follows from $\lambda _\mu (\xi )=\int _ X\xi $. These examples realize each integer jump $1,\ldots ,n$. A nonzero divisor with jump zero is given by $\theta =2h$ and $D=F_1$, since then the residual is still strictly positive. A fractional jump. Use the background $\beta =b\omega _1+q\omega _2$ of proposition 12.21.4 , where $q=|\zeta |^{2m}$ near its unique zero and $m>1$. Choose $c>0$ and put $\theta =\beta +c\omega _2>0$ and $D=c(E\times \{ w_0\} )$, whose smooth curvature form is $c\omega _2$. The original background is strictly positive, so both its orders are zero, whereas the residual has common order $1-1/m$. Unequal orders. Let $\beta _{\rm res}$ be the oscillatory rank-one background of proposition 12.21.5 , and put \[  \theta =\beta _{\rm res}+ch>0,\qquad D=c(\{ z_0\} \times E)+c(E\times \{ w_0\} ),\qquad \eta _ D=ch.  \] The background $\theta $ has both orders zero: since $\theta \geq ch$, every test quotient is bounded below by a positive constant, while one fixed test gives a finite upper bound. Its smooth nef residual is exactly $\beta _{\rm res}$, whose lower and upper orders differ. In each of these examples, the residual plus $[D]$ is a positive current in the smooth $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$-class of $\theta $, and its divisorial part is exactly $[D]$ because the residual is smooth. We do not need this current to have minimal singularities; that case is treated in corollary 12.24.5 . A residual that is not nef. Blow up $\mathbb P^2$ at two distinct points. Let $H$ be the pullback of the class of the normalized Fubini–Study form, let $E_1,E_2$ be the exceptional curves, and let $L$ be the strict transform of the line through the two points. The pullback $\theta $ of the Fubini–Study form is smooth, semipositive and nef. Subtract curvature forms of $D=E_1+E_2$. The residual $\beta $ has class $H-E_1-E_2$, which is the class of $L$, and the Poincaré–Lelong formula for the total transform of the line shows that it contains the positive current $[L]$. The intersection numbers $H^2=1$, $H\cdot E_ i=0$, $E_ i^2=-1$ and $E_1\cdot E_2=0$ give \[  \int _ L\beta =(H-E_1-E_2)^2=-1.  \] If $\beta $ were nef, smooth representatives $\beta +\epsilon h+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_\epsilon >0$ would give $-1+\epsilon \int _ Lh\geq 0$ for all $\epsilon >0$, which is impossible. $\square$ For a prime divisor $D$ and $\delta >0$, consider the infimum of the generic Lelong numbers along $D$ of the positive currents $\theta +\delta h+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$; its limit as $\delta \downarrow 0$ is the minimal multiplicity of $\theta $ along $D$. For a nef background all minimal multiplicities vanish, since every $\theta +\delta h$ has a smooth positive representative. Removing the divisor defined by these multiplicities therefore leaves a nef background unchanged. Removing the divisorial part of a particular positive current in the class of $\theta $ is a different operation, even when that current has minimal singularities. Corollary 12.24.5 . 9860E4D04E6C On the ruled surface $X$ of lemma 16.29.16 , keep its nef curvature form $\theta $, its section $D$ at infinity and its Kähler form $\kappa =\theta +\pi ^*\sigma _0$. For every smooth positive probability form $\mu $, \[  \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon \kappa )=2\epsilon (1+\epsilon ), \qquad \mathcal V_\mu (\epsilon \kappa )=2\epsilon ^2.  \] The only positive current of the form $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$ is $[D]$. It has minimal singularities, and removing its whole divisor leaves the zero background and changes the common order from one to two. Proof. Lemma 16.29.16 gives the uniqueness of $[D]$ and the nefness of $\theta $, and the calculation in the proof of proposition 16.29.18 gives $\int _ X\theta ^2=0$. Put $B=\pi ^*\sigma _0$. Then $B^2=0$, and \[  \int _ X\theta \wedge B=\int _ D B=1,  \] by the Poincaré–Lelong formula, Stokes' theorem and the fact that the section $D$ maps isomorphically onto the elliptic base. The closed nef formula following theorem 12.11.1 now computes both volumes by expanding the squares, for every $\mu $. Every $\theta $-plurisubharmonic function $u$ satisfies $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u=[D]$, so any two such functions differ by a pluriharmonic function, hence by a constant; in particular each has minimal singularities. Since $\theta $ is itself a curvature form of $\mathcal O_ X(D)$, removing the whole divisor leaves the zero background. The two volume polynomials give the orders one and two. $\square$

title: 12.25 Integer orders in fixed projective cones
search_title: Integer orders in fixed projective cones
section: 12.25 Integer orders in fixed projective cones
text: In the examples of section 12.21 the order is not an integer because a coefficient of the background vanishes at a point. We now consider backgrounds that are combinations, with strictly positive coefficient functions, of finitely many fixed closed semipositive generators on products of projective spaces and their linear blowups. Such backgrounds have integral orders even when they are not closed. The tool is a comparison with a closed semipositive form $B$ of constant rank. If $\theta $ is bounded above by a multiple of $B$ and, after the addition of a possibly singular potential, below by another multiple, then the Gauduchon quotients of $\theta +\epsilon h$ and of the closed form $B+\epsilon \Omega $ are comparable, and the latter have an explicit order. On a blown-up factor the pulled-back hyperplane form loses rank along the exceptional divisor, and the logarithmic potential of that divisor supplies the lower bound. Lemma 12.25.1 . DAA29135206D Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, let $\Omega $ be a Kähler form, and let $B$ be a smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-form. Suppose a smooth nef background $\theta $ satisfies \[  \theta \leq CB,\qquad \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq cB  \] as currents, for constants $c,C>0$ and a real function $\varphi \in L^1(X)$. For every Hermitian form $h$ and smooth strictly positive probability form $\mu $, there are constants $k,K>0$ such that, for $0<\epsilon \leq 1$, ED15CA2DA3FC 12.25.2 \begin{equation}  k\lambda _\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega ) \leq \lambda _\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) \leq K\lambda _\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega ). \end{equation} If $B$ has constant rank $R$, there are moreover constants $L,U>0$ with \[  L\epsilon ^{n-R}\leq \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) \leq U\epsilon ^{n-R},\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1.  \] In particular, $\theta $ then has common order $n-R$. Proof. Choose $c_ h,C_ h>0$ with $c_ h\Omega \leq h\leq C_ h\Omega $. For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $, distributional Stokes gives \[  \int _ X\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \wedge \gamma ^{n-1} =\langle \varphi ,\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\gamma ^{n-1}\rangle =0.  \] The lower bound for $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ therefore gives $\int _ X(\theta +\epsilon h)\wedge \gamma ^{n-1}\geq k\int _ X(B+\epsilon \Omega )\wedge \gamma ^{n-1}$ with $k=\min (c,c_ h)$, and the upper bound for $\theta $ gives the reverse inequality with $K=\max (C,C_ h)$. Dividing by $D_\mu (\gamma )>0$ and taking infima over all Gauduchon metrics proves ( 12.25.2 ); no rank hypothesis has been used. Now suppose that $B$ has constant rank $R$. Its $R$ positive eigenvalues relative to $\Omega $ are then bounded above and away from zero, uniformly on $X$. With $A_\epsilon =B+\epsilon \Omega $, compactness gives constants $m_0,M_0>0$ with 022F404D6957 12.25.3 \begin{equation}  m_0\epsilon ^{n-R}\mu \leq A_\epsilon ^ n \leq M_0\epsilon ^{n-R}\mu ,\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1. \end{equation} For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $, the pointwise arithmetic–geometric mean inequality gives \[  A_\epsilon \wedge \gamma ^{n-1} \geq \left(\frac{A_\epsilon ^ n}{\gamma ^ n}\right)^{1/n}\gamma ^ n,  \] and hence $\lambda _\mu (A_\epsilon )\geq m_0^{1/n}\epsilon ^{(n-R)/n}$. In the other direction, the positive closed form $\gamma =A_\epsilon $ is itself an admissible test. Writing $A_\epsilon ^ n=f_\epsilon \mu $, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  D_\mu (A_\epsilon )& =\int _ X f_\epsilon ^{(n-1)/n}\mu \geq m_0^{(n-1)/n}\epsilon ^{(n-R)(n-1)/n},\\  \int _ X A_\epsilon ^ n& \leq M_0\epsilon ^{n-R}, \end{aligned}  \] so the quotient of this test is at most $M_0m_0^{-(n-1)/n}\epsilon ^{(n-R)/n}$. Raising both bounds to the $n$th power and using ( 12.25.2 ) gives the two-sided power bounds. The argument includes $R=0$; when $n=1$, $D_\mu =1$. Fixed positive factors do not affect the order, since their logarithms are divided by $\log \epsilon $. $\square$

text: Lemma 12.25.1 . DAA29135206D Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, let $\Omega $ be a Kähler form, and let $B$ be a smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-form. Suppose a smooth nef background $\theta $ satisfies \[  \theta \leq CB,\qquad \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq cB  \] as currents, for constants $c,C>0$ and a real function $\varphi \in L^1(X)$. For every Hermitian form $h$ and smooth strictly positive probability form $\mu $, there are constants $k,K>0$ such that, for $0<\epsilon \leq 1$, ED15CA2DA3FC 12.25.2 \begin{equation}  k\lambda _\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega ) \leq \lambda _\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) \leq K\lambda _\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega ). \end{equation} If $B$ has constant rank $R$, there are moreover constants $L,U>0$ with \[  L\epsilon ^{n-R}\leq \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) \leq U\epsilon ^{n-R},\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1.  \] In particular, $\theta $ then has common order $n-R$. Proof. Choose $c_ h,C_ h>0$ with $c_ h\Omega \leq h\leq C_ h\Omega $. For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $, distributional Stokes gives \[  \int _ X\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \wedge \gamma ^{n-1} =\langle \varphi ,\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\gamma ^{n-1}\rangle =0.  \] The lower bound for $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi $ therefore gives $\int _ X(\theta +\epsilon h)\wedge \gamma ^{n-1}\geq k\int _ X(B+\epsilon \Omega )\wedge \gamma ^{n-1}$ with $k=\min (c,c_ h)$, and the upper bound for $\theta $ gives the reverse inequality with $K=\max (C,C_ h)$. Dividing by $D_\mu (\gamma )>0$ and taking infima over all Gauduchon metrics proves ( 12.25.2 ); no rank hypothesis has been used. Now suppose that $B$ has constant rank $R$. Its $R$ positive eigenvalues relative to $\Omega $ are then bounded above and away from zero, uniformly on $X$. With $A_\epsilon =B+\epsilon \Omega $, compactness gives constants $m_0,M_0>0$ with 022F404D6957 12.25.3 \begin{equation}  m_0\epsilon ^{n-R}\mu \leq A_\epsilon ^ n \leq M_0\epsilon ^{n-R}\mu ,\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1. \end{equation} For every Gauduchon metric $\gamma $, the pointwise arithmetic–geometric mean inequality gives \[  A_\epsilon \wedge \gamma ^{n-1} \geq \left(\frac{A_\epsilon ^ n}{\gamma ^ n}\right)^{1/n}\gamma ^ n,  \] and hence $\lambda _\mu (A_\epsilon )\geq m_0^{1/n}\epsilon ^{(n-R)/n}$. In the other direction, the positive closed form $\gamma =A_\epsilon $ is itself an admissible test. Writing $A_\epsilon ^ n=f_\epsilon \mu $, we have \[  \begin{aligned}  D_\mu (A_\epsilon )& =\int _ X f_\epsilon ^{(n-1)/n}\mu \geq m_0^{(n-1)/n}\epsilon ^{(n-R)(n-1)/n},\\  \int _ X A_\epsilon ^ n& \leq M_0\epsilon ^{n-R}, \end{aligned}  \] so the quotient of this test is at most $M_0m_0^{-(n-1)/n}\epsilon ^{(n-R)/n}$. Raising both bounds to the $n$th power and using ( 12.25.2 ) gives the two-sided power bounds. The argument includes $R=0$; when $n=1$, $D_\mu =1$. Fixed positive factors do not affect the order, since their logarithms are divided by $\log \epsilon $. $\square$

title: 12.25.4 Linear blowups and the fixed generators
search_title: Linear blowups and the fixed generators
section: 12.25 Integer orders in fixed projective cones
text: The manifolds are products of factors of two kinds. A plain factor is $Z_ i=\mathbb P^{m_ i}$ with $m_ i\geq 1$; let $H_ i$ be its Fubini–Study form normalized to have integral one on lines, and set $\kappa _ i=H_ i$. A blown-up factor is \[  Z_ i=\operatorname {Bl}_{\mathbb P^{\ell _ i}}\mathbb P^{m_ i}, \qquad m_ i\geq 2,\quad 0\leq \ell _ i\leq m_ i-2, \qquad r_ i=m_ i-\ell _ i-1,  \] the blowup of $\mathbb P^{m_ i}$ along a linear subspace of dimension $\ell _ i$. We describe one such factor and suppress the index for the moment. In homogeneous coordinates $[z_0:\cdots :z_\ell :w_0:\cdots :w_ r]$ on $\mathbb P^ m$, with the center $\{ w=0\} $, the blowup has the incidence model \[  Z=\{ (x,[t])\in \mathbb P^ m\times \mathbb P^ r: w_ at_ b=w_ bt_ a\text{ for all }a,b\} .  \] Let $p:Z\to \mathbb P^ m$ and $q:Z\to \mathbb P^ r$ be the projections. In the chart $t_ j=1$, the equations $w_ a=t_ aw_ j$ are the usual charts of the blowup along $\{ w_0=\cdots =w_ r=0\} $. Writing $w=\lambda t$ shows that $q$ is locally a $\mathbb P^{\ell +1}$-bundle, with fiber coordinates $[z:\lambda ]$. Thus $Z$ is smooth, $q$ is a submersion, and the incidence inclusion is an embedding. With $\omega _ m$ and $\omega _ r$ the normalized Fubini–Study forms on $\mathbb P^ m$ and $\mathbb P^ r$, set \[  H=p^*\omega _ m,\qquad Q=q^*\omega _ r,\qquad \kappa =H+Q.  \] The form $\kappa $ is Kähler, as the restriction of a product Kähler form, whereas $Q$ is semipositive of constant rank $r$. Let $E=\{ w=0\} $ be the exceptional divisor. The coordinate section $w_ j$ of $p^*\mathcal O(1)$ vanishes exactly on $E+q^{-1}\{ t_ j=0\} $, so $\mathcal O(E)=p^*\mathcal O(1)\otimes q^*\mathcal O(-1)$. Give this line bundle the product metric, whose curvature is $H-Q$. For its canonical section $s_ E$, the function $\psi _ E=\log |s_ E|^2$ is locally integrable, and the Poincaré–Lelong formula, as in section 12.35 , gives 00C606303647 12.25.5 \begin{equation}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi _ E=[E]-H+Q,\qquad H+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\psi _ E/2)=\tfrac 12(\kappa +[E])\geq \kappa /2. \end{equation} On $X=\prod _ i Z_ i$, put $n=\sum _ i m_ i$, and pull back all forms from the factors. Fix smooth strictly positive functions $f_ i$ on $X$, and, for each blown-up factor, a smooth strictly positive function $g_ i$ on $X$; these functions may depend on all coordinates of the product. The fixed cone consists of the backgrounds DE6D982F2E21 12.25.6 \begin{equation}  \theta =\sum _ i\bigl ((a_ i+b_ if_ i)H_ i+(c_ i+d_ ig_ i)Q_ i\bigr ), \qquad a_ i,b_ i,c_ i,d_ i\geq 0, \end{equation} where the terms involving $Q_ i$, and the parameters $c_ i,d_ i$, are omitted for plain factors. All coefficient functions and generators are fixed, and only the parameters vary. Every member of the cone is smooth and semipositive, hence nef. We say that $H_ i$ occurs in $\theta $ if $a_ i+b_ i>0$, and that $Q_ i$ occurs if $c_ i+d_ i>0$. Define EFE1F66045F4 12.25.7 \begin{equation}  R_ i(\theta )= \begin{cases}  m_ i,& \text{if }H_ i\text{ occurs},\\  r_ i,& \text{if }H_ i\text{ does not occur and }Q_ i\text{ occurs},\\  0,& \text{if neither occurs}, \end{cases} \qquad R(\theta )=\sum _ i R_ i(\theta ). \end{equation} The middle case can only occur on blown-up factors. Theorem 12.25.8 . 3F58257FA940 Every background $\theta $ in the fixed cone ( 12.25.6 ) has common order $n-R(\theta )$. More precisely, for every smooth positive probability form $\mu $ and Hermitian form $h$ there are constants $L,U>0$, depending on $\theta ,\mu ,h$, such that 79FA42084398 12.25.9 \begin{equation}  L\epsilon ^{n-R(\theta )} \leq \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) \leq U\epsilon ^{n-R(\theta )},\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1. \end{equation} Proof. Let $B_\theta $ be the sum of the forms $\kappa _ i$ over the factors in which $H_ i$ occurs and of the forms $Q_ i$ over the factors in which only $Q_ i$ occurs. It is closed and semipositive of constant rank $R(\theta )$. Since the coefficients are bounded and $H_ i,Q_ i\leq \kappa _ i$, we have $\theta \leq CB_\theta $ for some $C>0$. For the lower bound, let $s_ i=\min _ X(a_ i+b_ if_ i)>0$ for each blown-up factor in which $H_ i$ occurs, and put \[  \varphi =\sum _{\substack {i\text{ blown up}\\ H_ i\text{ occurs}}} (s_ i/2)\psi _{E_ i}.  \] By ( 12.25.5 ), $s_ iH_ i+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(s_ i\psi _{E_ i}/2)=(s_ i/2)(\kappa _ i+[E_ i])\geq (s_ i/2)\kappa _ i$. The remaining terms $(a_ i+b_ if_ i-s_ i)H_ i$ and all terms involving $Q_ i$ are semipositive. On plain factors in which $H_ i$ occurs and on factors in which only $Q_ i$ occurs, the relevant coefficient is bounded below by a positive constant. Taking the minimum of these constants gives $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq cB_\theta $ for some $c>0$. For $\theta =0$ take $\varphi =0$ and any $c>0$. Now apply lemma 12.25.1 with $\Omega =\sum _ i\kappa _ i$. $\square$ Members of the fixed cone need not be closed: by construction \[  \mathrm d\theta =\sum _ i b_ i\, \mathrm df_ i\wedge H_ i +\sum _{i\text{ blown up}}d_ i\, \mathrm dg_ i\wedge Q_ i.  \] If only one of these terms has a nonzero coefficient and the corresponding form, say $\mathrm df_ i\wedge H_ i$, is nonzero, then $\theta $ is not closed. On a blown-up factor, for instance, if $g$ is a small positive perturbation of a constant that varies along a fiber of $q$, then $\mathrm dg\wedge Q\ne 0$, since $r\geq 1$. On $\mathbb P^ p\times \mathbb P^ q$ with $p,q\geq 1$, a positive function $f$ that varies on the second factor gives the nonclosed background $fH_1$ of order $q$. Adding $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ of a smooth function does not change the exterior derivative.

title: 12.25.10 Equality of orders under modifications
section: 12.25 Integer orders in fixed projective cones
text: By proposition 12.22.5 , pulling back by a modification can only increase the orders. For the fixed cone, the orders are preserved. Proposition 12.25.11 . 57BC641DA62E Replacing some plain factors by linear blowups as above preserves the order of every background in the fixed cone. More generally, for every modification $\pi :Y\to X$ with $Y$ a compact Kähler manifold, the pullback $\pi ^*\theta $ has common order $n-R(\theta )$, and satisfies two-sided power bounds with this exponent for every smooth positive probability form and every Hermitian perturbation on $Y$. Proof. For a product of linear blowups, pull back the coefficient functions and take the new coefficients of the forms $Q_ i$ to be zero. A form $H_ i$ that occurs on a plain factor becomes a form $H_ i$ that occurs on a blown-up factor, with the same rank $m_ i$, and factors in which nothing occurs remain so. Hence theorem 12.25.8 , applied on both products, gives the same order. For a general compact Kähler manifold $Y$, pull back the semipositive smooth remainders and the divisor identities used in the proof above. Each nonzero holomorphic section remains nonzero under the surjective map $\pi $, and the logarithm of the squared norm of its pullback is locally integrable, with $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ equal to the current of its effective zero divisor minus the pulled-back curvature. Hence \[  \pi ^*\theta \leq C\pi ^*B_\theta ,\qquad \pi ^*\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(\varphi \circ \pi )\geq c\pi ^*B_\theta .  \] Fix a Kähler form $\Omega _ Y$ on $Y$, and apply the first part of lemma 12.25.1 , which needs no rank hypothesis; the pulled-back background is semipositive and hence nef. Put $R=R(\theta )$. Pullback does not increase rank, so $(\pi ^*B_\theta )^{R+1}=0$, while \[  \int _ Y(\pi ^*B_\theta )^ R\wedge \Omega _ Y^{n-R}>0:  \] for $R>0$ the integrand is positive on the nonempty set where $\pi $ is biholomorphic, and for $R=0$ the integral is the Kähler volume. For any smooth positive probability form $\mu _ Y$, the closed nef formula following theorem 12.11.1 gives \[  \mathcal V_{\mu _ Y}(\pi ^*B_\theta +\epsilon \Omega _ Y) =\sum _{k=0}^{R}\binom nk\epsilon ^{n-k} \int _ Y(\pi ^*B_\theta )^ k\wedge \Omega _ Y^{n-k}.  \] All coefficients are nonnegative and the coefficient for $k=R$ is positive, so this polynomial is bounded above and below by positive multiples of $\epsilon ^{n-R}$ for $0<\epsilon \leq 1$. The comparison of quotients gives the same bounds for $\pi ^*\theta +\epsilon h_ Y$. In particular, the order upstairs equals the order downstairs. $\square$

We now subtract effective divisors from members of the fixed cone. Let $\mathcal O(H_ i)$ and $\mathcal O(Q_ i)$ be the pullbacks of $\mathcal O(1)$ under the projections defining $H_ i$ and $Q_ i$, with their Fubini–Study metrics, whose curvature forms are $H_ i$ and $Q_ i$. Consider line bundles that are tensor products of integer powers of these bundles, negative powers included, and finite nonnegative real combinations of zero divisors of their nonzero holomorphic sections $s_
u $: \[   egin{gathered} D=\sum _

u \geq 0,\ \eta _ D=\sum _ i(\delta _ iH_ i+ho _ iQ_ i),\qquad \Phi _ D=\sum _

The terms involving $Q_ i$ are omitted for plain factors. Lemma 12.25.13 . 5DAA9B186CEE The coefficients $(\delta _ i,ho _ i)$ that occur for divisors $D$ of this form are exactly those satisfying \[  \delta _ i\geq 0	ext{ on plain factors};\qquad \delta _ i\geq 0,\quad \delta _ i+ho _ i\geq 0 	ext{ on blown-up factors}.  \] Proof. It suffices to treat one nonzero holomorphic section $s$, since nonnegative real combinations preserve the inequalities. Choose a point at which $s$ is nonzero and which lies outside all exceptional divisors, and fix the coordinates of the other factors. A projective line through that point inside a fiber of $q_ i$ has $H_ i$-degree one and $Q_ i$-degree zero. The restriction of $s$ to it is a nonzero section, so the exponent of $\mathcal O(H_ i)$ is nonnegative. On a plain factor, a line through the point gives the same inequality. On a blown-up factor, write the chosen point as $([z:w],[w])$ with $w
e 0$, and choose a linear map $A$ with $Aw=z$. The section of $q_ i$ given by $[t]\mapsto ([At:t],[t])$ passes through the point, and both $H_ i$ and $Q_ i$ have degree one on each projective line in its image. Such a line through the point exists because $r_ i\geq 1$, and $s$ restricts nontrivially to it. Its degree shows that the sum of the two exponents is nonnegative. Conversely, let $F_ i$ be the pullback under $q_ i$ of a hyperplane. An admissible pair $(\delta _ i,ho _ i)$ is realized by $\delta _ iE_ i+(\delta _ i+ho _ i)F_ i$, since $E_ i$ has curvature $H_ i-Q_ i$, and coefficients on plain factors are realized by hyperplanes. These are allowed nonnegative combinations and give every coefficient tuple in the stated range. $\square$ Theorem 12.25.14 . F79036F002E1 Let $	heta $ be in the fixed cone, with parameters $a_ i,b_ i,c_ i,d_ i$, and let $D$ be a divisor of the above form. Assume \[  a_ i\geq \delta _ i	ext{ for all }i,\qquad c_ i\geq ho _ i	ext{ for every blown-up factor}.  \] Then the residual $ eta =	heta -\eta _ D$ lies in the fixed cone, and the common orders $a( eta )$ and $a(	heta )$ satisfy \[  a( eta )-a(	heta )=\sum _ i igl (R_ i(	heta )-R_ i( eta ) igr )\geq 0.  \] Equality holds if and only if, for every factor,  egin{align*}  a_ i-\delta _ i+b_ i& >0& & 	ext{whenever }a_ i+b_ i>0,\  c_ i-ho _ i+d_ i& >0& & 	ext{whenever }a_ i=b_ i=0	ext{ and }c_ i+d_ i>0; \end{align*} the second condition concerns only blown-up factors. Proof. The residual parameters $(a_ i-\delta _ i,b_ i,c_ i-ho _ i,d_ i)$ are nonnegative, so $ eta $ lies in the fixed cone; in particular it is smooth, semipositive and nef. Also \[  (	heta - eta )+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ D=[D]\geq 0,  \] which is the positive-current comparison of proposition 12.24.1 . Apply theorem 12.25.8 to $	heta $ and to $ eta $. If $H_ i$ occurs in $	heta $ but not in $ eta $, the rank $R_ i$ drops from $m_ i$ to $r_ i<m_ i$ or to zero. If $H_ i$ does not occur in $	heta $, then $a_ i=b_ i=0$, and the range of lemma 12.25.13 together with $a_ i\geq \delta _ i$ forces $\delta _ i=0$ and hence $ho _ i\geq 0$; thus $Q_ i$ cannot appear in $ eta $ if it was absent from $	heta $. Therefore no rank $R_ i$ increases, each difference $R_ i(	heta )-R_ i( eta )$ is nonnegative, and the sum vanishes exactly when the generator that determines $R_ i(	heta )$ still occurs in $ eta $ for every $i$. This is the stated pair of conditions. $\square$ The parameter inequalities guarantee that the residual stays in the fixed cone; they do not describe all divisors whose residual is nef. Example 12.25.15 . EB3698E8A068 On $Z=\operatorname {Bl}_{\mathbb P^\ell }\mathbb P^ m$, choose a smooth function $g>0$ with $\mathrm dg\wedge Q
e 0$. For $t>0$, the nonclosed positive background $	heta _ t=tH+gQ$ has order zero. Removing $sE$, with its fixed curvature form $s(H-Q)$ and $0\leq s\leq t$, gives \[   eta _ s=(t-s)H+(g+s)Q,\qquad 	heta _ t+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(s\psi _ E)=s[E]+ eta _ s.  \] Every residual $ eta _ s$ is nef and not closed. Its order equals that of $	heta _ t$ exactly for $s<t$, and at $s=t$ the order jumps by $\ell +1$. These examples realize each integer jump $1,\ldots ,m-1$. Proof. The lower bound $	heta _ t\geq \min (t,\min g)\kappa >0$ shows that $	heta _ t$ is positive. For $s<t$ the form $H$ occurs in $ eta _ s$ and the rank is $m$; at $s=t$ only $Q$ occurs, with rank $r=m-\ell -1$. The order formula gives zero and $m-r=\ell +1$, respectively. The exterior derivative of every residual is $\mathrm dg\wedge Q
e 0$. Finally, let $\ell $ range from zero to $m-2$. $\square$ At the endpoint $s=t$, the current $t[E]+ eta _ t$ in the class of $	heta _ t$ has a divisorial part, although the minimal multiplicities of $	heta _ t$ vanish because $	heta _ t$ is nef, as explained before corollary 12.24.5 . title: Theorem 12.25.14
section: 12.25 Integer orders in fixed projective cones
text: Theorem 12.25.14 . F79036F002E1 Let $\theta $ be in the fixed cone, with parameters $a_ i,b_ i,c_ i,d_ i$, and let $D$ be a divisor of the above form. Assume \[  a_ i\geq \delta _ i\text{ for all }i,\qquad c_ i\geq \rho _ i\text{ for every blown-up factor}.  \] Then the residual $\beta =\theta -\eta _ D$ lies in the fixed cone, and the common orders $a(\beta )$ and $a(\theta )$ satisfy \[  a(\beta )-a(\theta )=\sum _ i\bigl (R_ i(\theta )-R_ i(\beta )\bigr )\geq 0.  \] Equality holds if and only if, for every factor, \begin{align*}  a_ i-\delta _ i+b_ i& >0& & \text{whenever }a_ i+b_ i>0,\\  c_ i-\rho _ i+d_ i& >0& & \text{whenever }a_ i=b_ i=0\text{ and }c_ i+d_ i>0; \end{align*} the second condition concerns only blown-up factors. Proof. The residual parameters $(a_ i-\delta _ i,b_ i,c_ i-\rho _ i,d_ i)$ are nonnegative, so $\beta $ lies in the fixed cone; in particular it is smooth, semipositive and nef. Also \[  (\theta -\beta )+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\Phi _ D=[D]\geq 0,  \] which is the positive-current comparison of proposition 12.24.1 . Apply theorem 12.25.8 to $\theta $ and to $\beta $. If $H_ i$ occurs in $\theta $ but not in $\beta $, the rank $R_ i$ drops from $m_ i$ to $r_ i<m_ i$ or to zero. If $H_ i$ does not occur in $\theta $, then $a_ i=b_ i=0$, and the range of lemma 12.25.13 together with $a_ i\geq \delta _ i$ forces $\delta _ i=0$ and hence $\rho _ i\geq 0$; thus $Q_ i$ cannot appear in $\beta $ if it was absent from $\theta $. Therefore no rank $R_ i$ increases, each difference $R_ i(\theta )-R_ i(\beta )$ is nonnegative, and the sum vanishes exactly when the generator that determines $R_ i(\theta )$ still occurs in $\beta $ for every $i$. This is the stated pair of conditions. $\square$

title: Example 12.25.15
section: 12.25 Integer orders in fixed projective cones
text: Example 12.25.15 . EB3698E8A068 On $Z=\operatorname {Bl}_{\mathbb P^\ell }\mathbb P^ m$, choose a smooth function $g>0$ with $\mathrm dg\wedge Q\ne 0$. For $t>0$, the nonclosed positive background $\theta _ t=tH+gQ$ has order zero. Removing $sE$, with its fixed curvature form $s(H-Q)$ and $0\leq s\leq t$, gives \[  \beta _ s=(t-s)H+(g+s)Q,\qquad \theta _ t+\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(s\psi _ E)=s[E]+\beta _ s.  \] Every residual $\beta _ s$ is nef and not closed. Its order equals that of $\theta _ t$ exactly for $s<t$, and at $s=t$ the order jumps by $\ell +1$. These examples realize each integer jump $1,\ldots ,m-1$. Proof. The lower bound $\theta _ t\geq \min (t,\min g)\kappa >0$ shows that $\theta _ t$ is positive. For $s<t$ the form $H$ occurs in $\beta _ s$ and the rank is $m$; at $s=t$ only $Q$ occurs, with rank $r=m-\ell -1$. The order formula gives zero and $m-r=\ell +1$, respectively. The exterior derivative of every residual is $\mathrm dg\wedge Q\ne 0$. Finally, let $\ell $ range from zero to $m-2$. $\square$

title: 12.26 A maximum-rank comparison criterion
text:
The constant-rank hypothesis in lemma 12.25.1 can be removed. For a closed semipositive form $B$, the intersection polynomial $\int _ X(B+\epsilon \Omega )^ n$ has a leading term of order $\epsilon ^{n-R}$, where $R$ is the largest rank that $B$ attains anywhere on $X$. Combined with the comparison of quotients, this gives the order $n-R$ for every background that is comparable to $B$. The criterion applies to backgrounds that vanish on an open set, and to positive variable multiples of arbitrary closed semipositive generators. Proposition 12.26.1 . 94DF4FEA70D3 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, let $B$ be a smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-form, and put $R=\max _ X\operatorname {rank}B$. Suppose a smooth nef background $	heta $ satisfies \[  	heta \leq CB,\qquad 	heta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq cB  \] as currents, for constants $c,C>0$ and a real function $\varphi \in L^1(X)$. For every smooth positive probability form $\mu $ and Hermitian form $h$, there are constants $L,U>0$ such that \[  L\epsilon ^{n-R}\leq \mathcal V_\mu (	heta +\epsilon h) \leq U\epsilon ^{n-R},\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1.  \] Thus $	heta $ has common order $n-R$, without any constant-rank hypothesis. Proof. Fix a Kähler form $\Omega $. The first part of lemma 12.25.1 , which does not use the rank, shows that $\lambda _\mu (	heta +\epsilon h)$ and $\lambda _\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega )$ differ by bounded positive factors. Since $B^{R+1}=0$, the closed nef formula following theorem 12.11.1 gives \[  \mathcal V_\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega ) =\sum _{k=0}^{R} inom nk\epsilon ^{n-k} \int _ X B^ k\wedge \Omega ^{n-k}.  \] All coefficients are nonnegative. If $R>0$, then at a point where $B$ has rank $R$, some $R	imes R$ minor of its coefficient matrix is positive and stays positive nearby, so $B^ R\wedge \Omega ^{n-R}$ has positive integral. If $R=0$, this integral is the Kähler volume. Hence the coefficient of $\epsilon ^{n-R}$ is positive. For $0<\epsilon \leq 1$, every other power of $\epsilon $ that occurs is at most $\epsilon ^{n-R}$, so the polynomial is bounded below by its leading term and above by the sum of its coefficients times $\epsilon ^{n-R}$. Raising the comparison of quotients to the $n$th power gives the asserted bounds, and taking logarithms gives the order. $\square$ Corollary 12.26.2 . 87EBA7661A8A On a compact Kähler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, fix finitely many smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-forms $B_ j$ and smooth strictly positive functions $f_ j$. For $t_ j\geq 0$, put \[  	heta =\sum _ jt_ jf_ jB_ j,\qquad B=\sum _{j:t_ j>0}B_ j,\qquad R=\max _ X\operatorname {rank}B.  \] The background $	heta $ is nef, has common order $n-R$, and satisfies the two-sided power bounds of proposition 12.26.1 . For every modification $\pi :Y	o X$ with $Y$ a compact Kähler manifold, the pullback $\pi ^*	heta $ has the same order and power bounds with the same exponent, for every smooth positive probability form and Hermitian perturbation on $Y$. Proof. Semipositivity gives nefness. If some $t_ j$ is positive, compactness and strict positivity of the functions $f_ j$ give \[   egin{gathered} cB\leq 	heta \leq CB,\qquad c=\min _{j:t_ j>0} igl (t_ j\min _ X f_ j igr )>0,\ C=\max _{j:t_ j>0} igl (t_ j\max _ X f_ j igr ), \end{gathered}  \] and proposition 12.26.1 applies with $\varphi =0$. If all parameters vanish, then $B=	heta =0$, $R=0$, any $c,C>0$ may be used, and the order is $n$. These inequalities between smooth forms are preserved by pullback, and the rank of $\pi ^*B$ is at most $R$. If $R>0$, the set where $B$ has rank $R$ is nonempty and open, so it meets the dense open set where $\pi $ is biholomorphic; hence the maximal rank of $\pi ^*B$ is $R$. This is immediate if $R=0$. Since $\dim Y=n$, the same proposition applies on $Y$, with any choice of data there. No singular potential needs to be pulled back. $\square$ The constants depend on the parameters $t_ j$ and need not stay bounded as a positive parameter tends to zero. The rank of a sum records how the generators overlap, and it need not equal the sum of their ranks. Members of the family are not closed when $\sum _ jt_ j\, \mathrm df_ j\wedge B_ j
e 0$. Example 12.26.3 . 698A2684C823 Let $X=\mathbb P^1	imes \mathbb P^ q$, $q\geq 1$, with projections $p_1,p_2$. Choose a smooth nonnegative function $b
ot\equiv 0$ on $\mathbb P^1$ that vanishes on a nonempty open set, and a smooth strictly positive nonconstant function $f$ on $\mathbb P^ q$. With $\omega _1$ the normalized Fubini–Study form on $\mathbb P^1$, set \[  B=p_1^*(b\omega _1),\qquad 	heta =(f\circ p_2)B.  \] The smooth nef background $	heta $ is not closed, vanishes on a nonempty open set, and has common order $q$, with two-sided bounds by multiples of $\epsilon ^ q$. Proof. The form $b\omega _1$ is closed, because the first factor is a curve, and semipositive. Its pullback has rank one where $b>0$ and rank zero where $b=0$, so its maximal rank is one. Since $n=q+1$, corollary 12.26.2 gives the order $q$. A nonconstant smooth function $f$ on the connected second factor has $\mathrm df
e 0$ somewhere. At a point of the product where $b>0$ and $\mathrm df
eq 0$, the horizontal two-form $B$ wedges nontrivially with the vertical one-form $p_2^*\mathrm df$. Thus $\mathrm d	heta =p_2^*\mathrm df\wedge B
e 0$. $\square$ These are geometric sufficient conditions for an integral common order, in the direction of 12.33.4 . They do not cover backgrounds without a closed semipositive comparison form, coefficient functions that are allowed to vanish, or the comparison of orders under residuals or non-Kähler modifications in general.

title: Proposition 12.26.1
text: Proposition 12.26.1 . 94DF4FEA70D3 Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, let $B$ be a smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-form, and put $R=\max _ X\operatorname {rank}B$. Suppose a smooth nef background $\theta $ satisfies \[  \theta \leq CB,\qquad \theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\varphi \geq cB  \] as currents, for constants $c,C>0$ and a real function $\varphi \in L^1(X)$. For every smooth positive probability form $\mu $ and Hermitian form $h$, there are constants $L,U>0$ such that \[  L\epsilon ^{n-R}\leq \mathcal V_\mu (\theta +\epsilon h) \leq U\epsilon ^{n-R},\qquad 0<\epsilon \leq 1.  \] Thus $\theta $ has common order $n-R$, without any constant-rank hypothesis. The first part of lemma 12.25.1 , which does not use the rank, shows that $\lambda _\mu (\theta +\epsilon h)$ and $\lambda _\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega )$ differ by bounded positive factors. Since $B^{R+1}=0$, the closed nef formula following theorem 12.11.1 gives \[  \mathcal V_\mu (B+\epsilon \Omega ) =\sum _{k=0}^{R}\binom nk\epsilon ^{n-k} \int _ X B^ k\wedge \Omega ^{n-k}.  \] All coefficients are nonnegative. If $R>0$, then at a point where $B$ has rank $R$, some $R\times R$ minor of its coefficient matrix is positive and stays positive nearby, so $B^ R\wedge \Omega ^{n-R}$ has positive integral. If $R=0$, this integral is the Kähler volume. Hence the coefficient of $\epsilon ^{n-R}$ is positive. For $0<\epsilon \leq 1$, every other power of $\epsilon $ that occurs is at most $\epsilon ^{n-R}$, so the polynomial is bounded below by its leading term and above by the sum of its coefficients times $\epsilon ^{n-R}$. title: Corollary 12.26.2
text: Corollary 12.26.2 . 87EBA7661A8A On a compact Kähler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, fix finitely many smooth closed semipositive $(1,1)$-forms $B_ j$ and smooth strictly positive functions $f_ j$. For $t_ j\geq 0$, put \[  \theta =\sum _ jt_ jf_ jB_ j,\qquad B=\sum _{j:t_ j>0}B_ j,\qquad R=\max _ X\operatorname {rank}B.  \] The background $\theta $ is nef, has common order $n-R$, and satisfies the two-sided power bounds of proposition 12.26.1 . For every modification $\pi :Y\to X$ with $Y$ a compact Kähler manifold, the pullback $\pi ^*\theta $ has the same order and power bounds with the same exponent, for every smooth positive probability form and Hermitian perturbation on $Y$. Proof. Semipositivity gives nefness. If some $t_ j$ is positive, compactness and strict positivity of the functions $f_ j$ give \[  \begin{gathered} cB\leq \theta \leq CB,\qquad c=\min _{j:t_ j>0}\bigl (t_ j\min _ X f_ j\bigr )>0,\\ C=\max _{j:t_ j>0}\bigl (t_ j\max _ X f_ j\bigr ), \end{gathered}  \] and proposition 12.26.1 applies with $\varphi =0$. If all parameters vanish, then $B=\theta =0$, $R=0$, any $c,C>0$ may be used, and the order is $n$. These inequalities between smooth forms are preserved by pullback, and the rank of $\pi ^*B$ is at most $R$. If $R>0$, the set where $B$ has rank $R$ is nonempty and open, so it meets the dense open set where $\pi $ is biholomorphic; hence the maximal rank of $\pi ^*B$ is $R$. This is immediate if $R=0$. Since $\dim Y=n$, the same proposition applies on $Y$, with any choice of data there. No singular potential needs to be pulled back. $\square$
